/-!
# TxGraffiti Conjecture 1: independence, annihilation, and residue

*Reference:* [arxiv/2507.17780](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780)
**In Reverie Together: Ten Years of Mathematical Discovery with a Machine
Collaborator** by *Randy Davila, Boris Brimkov, Ryan Pepper*

Conjecture 1, the oldest of the four TxGraffiti conjectures in the cited
collection (open since 2016), asserts that every nontrivial connected graph $G$
with maximum degree $\Delta \ge 2$ satisfies
$$\alpha(G) \ge \frac{a(G) + R(G)}{\Delta(G)},$$
where $\alpha$ is the independence number, $a$ the annihilation number, $R$ the
Havel–Hakimi residue, and $\Delta$ the maximum degree.

This conjecture is **true**, proved in
[arXiv:2606.29553](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29553) (C. Gupta).
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Arxiv.«2507.17780»

/--
TxGraffiti [Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780):
for every nontrivial connected graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \ge 2$,
$$\alpha(G) \ge \frac{a(G) + R(G)}{\Delta(G)}.$$

This conjecture is **true**.

**Proof sketch.** Substitute the Caro–Wei lower bound $\alpha \ge W$ for $\alpha$
and reduce to $a \le (\Delta - 1) \alpha$. The case $\Delta = 2$ is trivial
($a = \alpha$). For $\Delta \ge 4$ an AM–HM argument with $m \le (n - a)\Delta$
yields a quadratic whose discriminant is negative. For $\Delta = 3$ the
annihilation number has a closed form in the degree counts $(n_1, n_2, n_3)$ and
$a \le 2W$ is verified in three regimes. See
[arXiv:2606.29553](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29553).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem tx_graffiti_conjecture_1 (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (_hConn : G.Connected)
    (_hDeg : 2 ≤ G.maxDegree) :
    (G.annihilationNumber + residue G : ℝ) / G.maxDegree ≤ G.indepNum := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«2507.17780»

reformulations.difference: The imported definition maximizes cardinality over all degree submultisets with sum at most the edge count, whereas the paper uses the largest feasible prefix of the increasingly sorted degrees.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Among all selections of j degree entries, the j smallest have minimal sum. Thus a feasible j-element submultiset exists exactly when the j-smallest-degree prefix is feasible. Their maximum feasible cardinalities coincide. This was proved generally and specialized to graphs in /workspace/review/annihilation_equiv.lean, including an explicit equivalence lemma, without using the conjecture or the unproved annihilationNumberEq helper.

reformulations.difference: The declaration states the inequality without a separate assertion that the bound is sharp.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Sharpness has an independently verifiable witness: K₄ is connected, has Δ = 3, a = 2, R = 1, and α = 1, so (a + R)/Δ = α. Consequently adding the sharpness conjunct does not strengthen the problem. The witness and the equivalence P ↔ (P ∧ sharpness) were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture.

review.notes: The theorem faithfully states the corrected version in Gupta's Theorem 2. The original 2025 Conjecture 1 lacks Δ ≥ 2 and fails on K₂; Gupta explicitly identifies this exception and proves precisely the restricted statement used here. Thus the degree hypothesis is supported by the second cited source, and the research solved tag agrees with it. Checked all invariant definitions, quantifiers, hypotheses, casts, and boundary cases. Lean proofs establish that the hypotheses force at least three vertices and that the real quotient inequality is equivalent to the source's product inequality. Tests covered empty graphs, complete graphs, paths, cycles, and stars. Exhaustive evaluation of all 1,100 labelled simple graphs on zero through five vertices found no annihilation-definition discrepancies; all 770 graphs satisfying the theorem's hypotheses passed the inequality check. All experiments are under /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file remains unchanged.
